liveEngine.note: Every item below was run through the UNMODIFIED live engine. These six slices are GAPS: each positive is an authentic VN->EN learner error the engine currently ABSTAINS on (no rule fires), and every confusable negative correctly ABSTAINS. Slices already covered by the wired en-step5-preposition-pattern / en-step6-* rules (e.g. depend-of->on, good-in->at, listen-to, wait-for, discuss-about, marry-with, look-at) were deliberately EXCLUDED to avoid overlap with in-flight Lane A work.

items.description: VN 'so' takes no fixed preposition, so learners attach the wrong one: afraid + from/with + <fear noun> should be afraid OF + <fear noun>.
items.detectorSketch: Fire only on the adjective 'afraid' immediately followed by 'from' or 'with' and then a noun phrase naming the thing feared. Rewrite the preposition to 'of'. Do NOT fire when 'afraid' is followed by a clause ('afraid (that) I can't ...') or by 'of'.
items.fp_risk_note: Medium-high. 'I'm afraid I can't come' is a politeness idiom (afraid + clause) and must never be touched. Restrict to the {from, with} -> of rewrite where the head after the preposition is a concrete/abstract fear object, not a finite clause.

positive.notes: GAP: engine abstains today; proposed correction shown.

items.description: VN 'den' (to/arrive) makes learners say 'arrive TO <place>'. English uses 'arrive at' (point/venue), 'arrive in' (city/country), and NO preposition before home/here/there.
items.detectorSketch: Fire on the verb 'arrive(d)' + 'to' + place. Rewrite: 'to' -> 'at' for venues/points, 'to' -> 'in' for cities/countries, and DROP 'to' entirely before home/here/there. Do NOT fire when 'arrive' already uses at/in or has no preposition.
items.fp_risk_note: High. The correct preposition is object-dependent (at venue / in city / none for home). A naive 'to'->'at' insert is wrong for 'arrive in Hanoi' and 'arrive home'. Requires a place-type classifier; ship at/in/none variants rather than a single fixed preposition.

positive.notes: GAP: 'home' takes NO preposition — drop 'to'. Engine abstains today.

items.description: VN 'giai thich cho toi' (explain for/to me) maps to a double-object pattern learners over-apply: 'explain me the X'. English 'explain' is not ditransitive — it must be 'explain the X to me'.
items.detectorSketch: Fire on 'explain' + <pronoun/person> + <noun phrase> (no 'to'). Rewrite to 'explain <noun phrase> to <pronoun/person>'. Do NOT fire when 'to' is already present, or when there is no recipient ('explain the problem').
items.fp_risk_note: Medium. Must not touch the already-correct 'explain X to me' or recipient-less 'explain the problem'. Anchor on the explain + bare-recipient + object shape; verbs that ARE ditransitive (give/send/tell) must not be swept in.

items.description: VN 'tra loi cho/voi' leads learners to over-insert 'to' after the verb 'answer': 'answer TO my question'. The transitive verb takes a direct object: 'answer my question'.
items.detectorSketch: Fire on the VERB 'answer' + 'to' + <question/email/message/me/you/etc.> in the 'respond' sense; delete 'to'. Do NOT fire on the NOUN 'the answer to X', nor on the accountability idiom 'answer to your boss', nor on other verbs ('reply to' is correct).
items.fp_risk_note: High. 'answer to' is valid as a noun complement ('the answer to the question') and as a phrasal verb meaning 'be accountable to' ('you answer to me now'). Requires verb-sense disambiguation; only the respond-sense transitive 'answer to <message/question/person>' should drop 'to'.

items.description: VN 'don' (fetch someone) is single-word, so learners drop the particle: 'pick me at school' instead of the phrasal 'pick me up'. The transport/fetch sense requires the 'up' particle.
items.detectorSketch: Fire on 'pick' + <person/pronoun object> + <at/from + place | at + time> with NO 'up'. Insert 'up' after the object: 'pick <obj> up <rest>'. Do NOT fire on 'pick' meaning select ('pick a flower/card/number') or when 'up' is already present.
items.fp_risk_note: High. 'pick' also means choose ('I picked a flower', 'pick a card') and must keep no particle. Anchor strictly on the fetch-a-person frame (animate object + locative/temporal adjunct) before inserting 'up'.

items.description: VN 'len xe / xuong xe' (up vehicle / down vehicle) calques to 'go up/down the bus'. English boarding uses 'get on' (board) and 'get off' (alight) for public/large vehicles.
items.detectorSketch: Fire on 'go up' + <vehicle> -> 'get on' + <vehicle>, and 'go down' + <vehicle> -> 'get off' + <vehicle>, restricted to a vehicle whitelist (bus, train, plane, boat, ferry, subway, tram, bike, motorbike). Do NOT fire on 'go up/down the stairs/hill/ladder/street/mountain'.
items.fp_risk_note: High. 'go up/down' is correct for stairs, hills, ladders, streets, mountains. Gate strictly on a transport-noun whitelist as the direct object; never on inclines or paths. (Note: 'get in/out of' is the idiom for cars/taxis — keep cars OUT of this 'get on/off' slice.)
